page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and provides 4 dedicated physical cores. With simultaneous multithreading active at two threads per core, the configuration yields 8 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 32.0 GB of total system RAM.

The hardware configuration maintains a balanced resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual CPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, which means persistent operating systems and data partitions must utilize attached network storage volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs bundled in this profile. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

This server type is engineered for reliable general computing tasks where balanced CPU and memory allocations are necessary without the added overhead of local NVMe arrays or GPU hardware. Typical operational profiles include running web application tiers, API endpoints, microservices, continuous integration agents, and standard enterprise business services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose compute instance based on the AMD EPYC 9J14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated virtual CPUs clocked at 2.3 GHz with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, establishing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The VM contains no onboard local disk storage and lacks GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage solutions for persistent data workloads. In addition, each instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By delivering dedicated x86 compute capacity without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators or localized NVMe arrays, this configuration offers a cost-effective platform for standard enterprise applications, container orchestration nodes, backend web servers, development environments, and moderate distributed data processing services.
